# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 1

**1** This is the vision I saw, brothers and sisters: **2** After I had fasted for many days and been praying earnestly, asking God to reveal what he had promised me through the aged woman — that very night the aged woman appeared to me and said, "Because you hunger so greatly and are so eager for knowledge, come early in the morning to the field where you farm, and at the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you need to see." **3** I asked her, "Lady, in which part of the field?" She replied, "Wherever you like." I chose a peaceful, suitable spot. But before I could say anything further to tell her where it was, she said, "I will come wherever you wish." **4** So I went out to the field, brothers and sisters, counted the hours, and arrived at the place I had designated. And I saw an ivory couch set there, on which lay a linen cushion and over it a covering of fine linen. **5** When I saw these things lying there with no one in the place, I was overcome with astonishment, and a trembling came upon me and my hair rose on end. And since I was there alone and had grown frightened, I pulled myself together and regained my composure. Then I saw the aged woman approaching with a small book in her hand; she sat down alone and greeted me: "Greetings, Hermas." **6** I replied in grief and weeping, "Greetings, my lady." She asked me, "Why so sad and downcast, Hermas? You are patient and even-tempered and always cheerful." I said, "On account of an excellent woman who says I have sinned against her." **7** She said, "Far be such a thing from a servant of God! Nevertheless, that thought did arise in your heart. Such thoughts are precisely what bring sin upon the servants of God. For it is an evil and shameful purpose for a righteous person to harbor a wicked desire — and all the more so for Hermas, who is temperate and abstains from every wicked desire and is characterized by simplicity and great innocence." **8** "But God is not angry with you for this alone — it is also to bring your household to repentance, since they have sinned against the Lord and against you their parents. Yet you love your children and failed to discipline your household, and that is why the Lord is displeased with you. Nevertheless he will heal all the former failures of your household, for through their sins and transgressions you have been worn down by the anxieties of this age. But the great mercy of the Lord has shown compassion on you, and will establish you and your household, and strengthen you before his glory."

---

*LOGOS note: "fifth hour" = approximately 11 AM; the repeated material from Vision 1 establishes the recurring structure of divine confirmation.*
